newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity futures mixed in moderate volume.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity futures mixed in moderate volume.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures were trading mixed in moderate volume with February California Oregon Border (COB) prices moving higher on an increase in Bonneville Power Administration prices, industry sources said.
As of 1300 EST, February COB was trading up 55 cents at $14.25 after morning exchanges in a range of $13.80-14.50 per megawatt hour (MWh).

The Bonneville Power Administraton (BPA) said Monday it was raising its offer price for firm power during heavy load hours on Tuesday to as high as $46.00 per MWh, nearly tripling the price of offers from late last week.
A source at BPA attributed the offer to higher daytime regional power demand and limitations on drafting from hydroelectric reservoirs.
March COB had not traded but was bid at $12.30 and offered at $12.60 from Friday's settle at $12.85 per MWh.
February Palo Verde (PV) had traded down 10 cents at $16.45 per MWh, while March PV was bid at $14.25 and offered at $14.90 from Friday's settlement at $14.85 per MWh.
NYMEX said as of 1240 EST an estimated 113 COB and 11 PV contracts had traded.
